title: JavaScript Runtime and Data Phase Assessment
description: Comprehensive phase-end assessment covering all lessons in JavaScript Runtime and Data.

questions.prompt: A program needs to apply const and let. Which approach is most reliable?

options.text: declare stable bindings with const and state that changes with let
const does not make a referenced object deeply immutable

questions.explanation: declare stable bindings with const and state that changes with let. Verify this behavior with a minimal runnable example and observable output.

questions.prompt: A program needs to apply typeof. Which approach is most reliable?

options.text: use typeof while diagnosing values at an input boundary

questions.explanation: use typeof while diagnosing values at an input boundary. Verify this behavior with a minimal runnable example and observable output.

questions.prompt: A program needs to apply Number conversion. Which approach is most reliable?

options.text: convert then check Number.isNaN before arithmetic
Number('') produces zero, which may require separate empty-input validation

questions.explanation: convert then check Number.isNaN before arithmetic. Verify this behavior with a minimal runnable example and observable output.

questions.prompt: A program needs to apply strict equality. Which approach is most reliable?

options.text: use strict equality for predictable branch conditions
0 == false is true but 0 === false is false

questions.explanation: use strict equality for predictable branch conditions. Verify this behavior with a minimal runnable example and observable output.

questions.prompt: A program needs to apply template literals. Which approach is most reliable?

options.text: use template literals for readable calculated output
ordinary quoted strings do not interpolate ${expressions}

questions.explanation: use template literals for readable calculated output. Verify this behavior with a minimal runnable example and observable output.
